title: Limiter Heartbeat Protocol and Deterministic Burst Rehydration for Multi-Region Failover
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: During recent multi-region incidents we observed two failure modes for quota enforcement: (1) limiter control-plane partitions that cause nodes to stop receiving global lease updates and later rehydrate with stale local state, producing traffic spikes; (2) transparent client failover that shifts bursts into a single region where local buckets are drained quickly and the downstream limiter becomes a blackhole until state reconciliation completes. Goal: implement a protocol and deterministic rehydration algorithm so that when limiter control connectivity is interrupted and later restored, the system reconciles outstanding usage without producing a sudden spike that violates SLOs or exhausts downstream capacity. This ticket covers designing the protocol, implementing a prototype in the limiter service, writing integration tests (simulations + chaos), and a safe rollout path with observable guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Limiter nodes exchange compact heartbeat leases (epoch + last-consume-seq + unit-hash) and can deterministically compute a reconciled global consumption value after partition recovery
Post-recovery traffic spike measured in integration tests must be <= 10% of steady-state burst capacity for the same workload shape
No customer token is double-counted during reconnection windows in the simulation harness and deterministic reconcilers pass property-based checks
Fail-open fallback for control-plane outages is limited by a local decay/backoff curve and a global emergency shed policy; verification tests exist
Rollout can be toggled via feature flag and has per-tenant telemetry (reconciled_consumed, reconciliation_delta, rehydrate_blocked_count)
Design reviewed and approved by Reliability and Product; security review flagged and mitigations documented
design_notes: Overview: introduce a lightweight heartbeat lease protocol between limiter replicas and an authoritative cross-region reconciler. Each limiter maintains a monotonic epoch and a local sequence (consume_seq) that increments on every token grant. Heartbeat payload = {epoch, last_consume_seq, local_sentinel_hash} — small and idempotent.

Deterministic Rehydration: upon reconnect, the reconciler gathers heartbeats across replicas for an epoch window and computes global_consumed = max(per-replica-last_consume_seq_adjusted) where adjusted adds conservative drain_estimates for disconnected intervals. The reconciler then issues a signed rehydrate_token (epoch, reconciled_consumed, signature) used to clamp local buckets so they never expose more tokens than the reconciled amount.

Epoch Management: epochs are advanced by the allocator service when topology changes (failover, shuffle). Nodes continue to process requests during partition with local epoch; when reconnecting, if node's epoch < reconciler_epoch, node must accept rehydrate token and apply clamp logic before granting further tokens.

Conservative Estimation: for disconnected windows we use a deterministic decay model: estimated_extra = min(max_per_second * disconnected_seconds, burst_cap) to avoid underestimating consumption. The decay constants are configurable per-tenant based on historical p95 request rates.

Blackhole Detection: if a node's heartbeat stops and we observe request backlog or increased latency upstream, mark node as potential blackhole. Blackhole nodes enter a strict local throttle (max 10% of normal throughput) until rehydration completes or node is evicted by allocator.

Fail-Open Policy: short control-plane outages should not automatically open unlimited capacity. We implement a client-visible retry-suggest header and a local exponential backoff (client-facing) to spread retries. Emergency global shed is triggered when reconciled_consumed_delta across tenants exceeds configured threshold.
Security and Integrity: rehydrate tokens are HMAC signed using control-plane keys (rotated) to prevent tampering. Heartbeats exclude PII and only include aggregated counters and sentinel hashes.

Compatibility: design is additive. Existing token bucket logic remains; reconcilers operate as a gating layer that can clamp or authorize extra token grants. Feature is feature-flagged per deployment and per-tenant for staged rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary: implement feature flag; run in canary region behind a toggle that only affects internal tenants. Simulate partitions with chaos monkey (network partitions + delayed heartbeats). Validate reconciliation metrics.
Phase 1 - Controlled Beta: enable for low-traffic external tenants (opt-in). Monitor reconciled_delta and throttle_events. Run 72h soak.
Phase 2 - Gradual Rollout: ramp to 50% of production traffic over 7 days with auto-rollback if reconcilation_delta > threshold or error rate increases by >0.5% absolute.
Phase 3 - Global Enforce: enable by default and remove feature flag after 4 weeks of stable metrics. Publish runbook and postmortem template for any reconciliation-related incidents.
Rollback: per-tenant flag and emergency kill-switch in console; disable reconciler and fall back to previous limiter behaviour (local-only) when triggered
telemetry_and_alerts: New metrics: reconciler.reconciled_consumed (gauge per-tenant), reconciler.reconciliation_delta (histogram), limiter.local_blocked_during_rehydrate (counter), limiter.heartbeat_lag_seconds (gauge)
Dashboards: Reconciliation summary (by region) with heatmap of reconciliation_delta and per-tenant anomalies
Alerts: P0 when global reconciliation_delta in any region > 2x configured tenant burst_cap for >5 minutes; P1 when reconciler error-rate > 1% for 10m
SLOs impacted: track 99th latency and 99.9th success rate during recovery windows; set temporary SLO burn budget alerts

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-conservative reconciliation could permanently block legitimate traffic. Mitigation: allow emergency bypass for quota admins and monitor reconciliation_delta trends with a slow ramp-up policy.

Risk: Reconciler becomes single point of throttling. Mitigation: run reconciler as a replicated stateless worker with small in-memory caches and ensure it can be autoscaled during reconstructions; add circuit breaker around reconciler calls to fallback to conservative local policy.

Risk: Misconfiguration of decay constants per-tenant. Mitigation: default to safe low-throughput decay and provide a calibration job that computes tenant-specific decay values from historical p95 rates.
Risk: Attack surface from heartbeat signatures. Mitigation: rotate keys, minimal payload, and audit logs for rehydrate token issuance.
